items.title: Two workflow steps still on older versions
items.summary: The checkout and Node setup steps of the publishing workflow are on version 5 while version 7 of both is out.
detail: The workflow that tests PLEX and publishes it uses checkout v5 and setup-node v5. The newest published versions are checkout v7 and setup-node v7.

They still work, but older major versions stop getting fixes and GitHub eventually retires the runtimes they are built on. This week showed what that looks like: the publish step broke on its own (see the next card).
How: change both version numbers in .github/workflows/pages.yml, read the release notes for changed inputs, push, and confirm the run is green. Effort: about 20 minutes.

items.title: Test tool is two releases behind
items.summary: The app's automatic tests are pinned to Playwright 1.63.0 while 1.65.1 is the current release.
detail: Playwright is the tool that opens the app in a simulated iPhone and desktop browser and checks every page before publishing. All 34 tests pass today on 1.63.0.
Newer versions bring newer browser builds, so the tests stay closer to what Edge and Safari actually do. Staying many versions behind makes the eventual jump harder.
How: set @playwright/test to 1.65.1 in package.json, run npm install, run the tests, commit package.json and package-lock.json together. Effort: 15 minutes.

items.title: Publishing to phones repaired
items.summary: The publish step had stopped finding the uploaded site, so the three GitHub Pages steps were moved to their current versions and publishing works again.
detail: During this run the tests passed but the final publish step (deploy-pages version 4) failed twice, reporting that it could not find the uploaded site package although the package was there. Earlier runs the same day had worked, so the cause was on GitHub's side, not in PLEX.
The workflow now uses deploy-pages v5, upload-pages-artifact v5 and configure-pages v6. The next run tested and published successfully, so phones receive this week's version.
Nothing to do; this note is only so the change is not a surprise in the workflow file.

items.title: Ollama now uses Intel graphics out of the box
items.summary: Since version 0.30 Ollama switches on Vulkan graphics acceleration by default, which covers Intel integrated and Arc graphics.
detail: Ollama is the optional local model runner behind Ask PLEX on the laptop. Its June 2026 release turned on Vulkan by default, so AMD and Intel graphics are used without extra vendor libraries. The same release improved loading of GGUF model files through llama.cpp.
For PLEX this means Ask PLEX answers can run on the laptop's Intel graphics instead of only the processor, which usually gives quicker replies and leaves the processor free for the rest of the app.

How: update Ollama on the laptop to 0.30 or later, run a short question and watch the graphics load in Task Manager. A GGUF file copied onto the laptop can be added offline with a one-line Modelfile (FROM ./file.gguf) and ollama create. The sources give no speed figures for Intel graphics, so time a few typical questions before and after. Effort: under an hour.

links.title: Ollama blog – Improved performance and model support with GGUF
AlternativeTo – Ollama 0.30 delivers wider hardware support

items.title: OpenVINO 2026.3/2026.4: bigger models on 16 GB
items.summary: Intel's OpenVINO can now keep part of a large mixture-of-experts model on disk, so a 30-billion-parameter Qwen model runs on a 16 GB machine.
detail: OpenVINO is Intel's own engine for running models on Intel processors, graphics and the NPU. Version 2026.3 (August 2026) added disk offloading for mixture-of-experts models; Intel says this lets Qwen3-30B-A3B work on systems with 16 GB of memory. Version 2026.4 (September 2026) made Gemma 4 faster on Intel graphics and added faster guessing-ahead decoding for Gemma 4 and Qwen3.5/3.6.
For PLEX this is the alternative to Ollama when answers need a stronger model than the small ones that fit fully in memory, for example summarising a whole week of reports.

Caution from the release notes: some NPU drivers crash; Intel recommends NPU driver 32.0.100.5540 or later. Try it on the laptop as a side test before relying on it. Effort: half a day to install and compare with Ollama.

links.title: Edge AI and Vision Alliance – Intel releases OpenVINO 2026.3

items.title: Hidden-risk tagging of report remarks
items.summary: Operators now use small fine-tuned language models to find risks written into report lines that were booked as productive time.
detail: SLB describes tagging daily drilling report remarks into 13 risk classes, aimed at lines coded as normal operations that still describe a problem. A fine-tuned 7-billion-parameter model agreed with engineers on 94% of 342 checked remarks from 180 reports (about 96% after a second review). At the IADC technology forum in March 2026, a talk on retrieval-based IADC code assignment across four rigs reported more than half the report preparation time saved.
For PLEX this fits the invisible lost time analytics: lines booked as productive but mentioning waiting, repeat runs, or equipment trouble are exactly where invisible lost time hides.

How: keep a fixed list of risk tags, hand-label a few hundred past remarks once, then let the local model (Ollama) suggest a tag for each new line with those labelled examples in the prompt. Show suggestions for the Company Man to accept or reject and feed the answers back into the examples. Effort: two to three days.

links.title: SLB – Extracting drilling risks from daily drilling reports using generative AI
IADC Drilling Engineering Committee Q1 2026 forum proceedings

items.title: Data audit and job pace with conformal limits
items.summary: Conformal control limits flag an unusual job time or data value without assuming the numbers follow a bell curve.
detail: A December 2025 paper shows how to build control-chart limits from a set of past normal values: score each value by its distance from the median, and take the matching rank as the alarm limit. Any new value gets a p-value, a simple 0 to 1 measure of how unusual it is compared with the past.

For PLEX this suits small data: the hourly data audit and the learning loop for job pace have tens of past jobs, not thousands. Each new casing run, trip or BOP test can be scored against its own past jobs, and flagged when it falls outside the band instead of using a fixed percentage.

How: for each job type keep the last 20 to 30 durations, compute the median and sorted distances, and show the band (for example 90%) on the lookahead and an alert when a value falls outside it. The author warns that the band is only as good as the past jobs chosen, so exclude jobs with known breakdowns. Effort: one day in the engine.

links.title: arXiv – Distribution-free process monitoring with conformal prediction

items.title: iPhone: any page can be a home-screen app
items.summary: Since iOS 26, Safari opens anything added to the home screen as a full-screen web app and also supports WebGPU.
detail: With iOS and iPadOS 26, adding a site to the home screen opens it as a web app by default; a manifest and service worker are no longer needed for that. Safari 26 also added WebGPU (graphics-card computing in the browser) and the File System WritableStream API for writing files.

For PLEX the bridge report page and the upload page can each be added as their own home-screen icon on the bridge and store phones, opening straight to the form without the main app. WebGPU on iPhone also makes in-browser models possible later: Transformers.js version 4 runs models on WebGPU and can cache them for offline use after the first download.

How: send the bridge team the report link and ask them to use Share › Add to Home Screen with Open as web app switched on. In-browser models are a later experiment, not urgent. Effort: minutes for the icons.

links.title: heise – iOS 26: changed web app behaviour on the home screen

items.title: Apps Script: no quota changes this quarter
items.summary: Google's Apps Script release notes since August 2026 list no quota, Gmail, Drive or Sheets changes that affect PLEX Cloud.
detail: The only Apps Script entries since August 2026 are the Gemini helper panel in the script editor (generally available in November) and data-region controls for Enterprise Plus and some education accounts (September). Data regions do not apply to an ordinary personal account.
For PLEX Cloud nothing needs to change. The Gemini panel can help when editing the script, but suggestions must be read before accepting, since the script holds access checks.
Effort: none.
